[center][img]https://i.imgur.com/KWaN3jU.png[/img][/center]
Machine Progression System adds [b]new tiered upgrades to the artisan and refining equipment[/b] in Stardew Valley. These upgrades allow you to [b]improve your machines[/b] in a variety of ways. Through an [b]extensive configuration system [/b]provided by [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/5098]Generic Mod Config Menu[/url], you can:
[list]
[*]Fully customize [b]processing times[/b], input and output [b]quantities[/b], and the [b]quality[/b] of the final products.[/*]
[*]Choose whether machines should [b]copy the quality[/b] of the input item.[/*]
[*]Unlock new, goal-based [b]production bonuses[/b] as you progress.[/*]
[*]Access entirely [b]new and exciting features[/b] unique to Machine Progression System.[/*]
[*]Create and configure over [b]50 new products[/b], designed to rebalance underused processes and support entirely new playstyles.[/*]
[/list]
The Machine Progression System features [b]six upgrade tiers[/b]: [b]Stee[/b]l, [b]Gold[/b], [b]Diamond[/b], [b]Iridium[/b], [b]Radioactive [/b]and [b]Prismatic[/b]. With the Upgrade Packs introduced by [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/users/41850015]tlitookilakin[/url]'s incredible [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/33024][b]Machine Upgrade System[/b][/url], players can [b]upgrade their machines[/b] and unlock all the benefits mentioned above. The Machine Upgrade System also allows for [b]extensive customization[/b] of the upgrade process, giving you full control over the system. You can:
[list]
[*]Choose the [b]amounts of resources needed[/b] to craft an upgrade pack, allowing you to [b]customize the difficulty[/b] to your preference.[/*]
[*]Change the [b]resources required[/b] to craft each upgrade, giving you control over the [b]materials you wish to use[/b]. [/*]
[/list]

Thanks to [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/users/41850015]tlitookilakin[/url]'s amazing [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/33024][b]Machine Upgrade System[/b][/url], upgrading machines is now easier than ever. Here is how it works:
[list=1]
[*][b]Unlock the base recipe[/b]. Before upgrading a machine, you must unlock its base recipe. For example, you cannot upgrade a Keg until you reach Farming level 8.[/*]
[*][b]Craft an Upgrade Pack[/b]. Open your Crafting Menu and craft the appropriate Upgrade Pack. To find out which one you need, simply hover over the machine.[/*]
[*][b]Apply the Upgrade Pack[/b]. You can apply the Upgrade Pack [b]d[/b][b]irectly[/b] on the machine placed in the world or while the machine is in your [b]inventory.[/b][/*]
[/list]

[center][b][size=4]Cask[/size][/b]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/uEELivz.png[/img][/center]
[spoiler]
[quote][b]Casks[/b] age products. Aging means [b]increasing a product's quality[/b]. These casks can be [b]placed everywhere[/b]. [/quote]
[b]3.0 Features[/b]
Casks can now age every Artisan Product and a few more items. These items are divided into four groups, depending on their aging speed. 
[list]
[*][b]Group 1[/b] (the slowest): Dried Fruit, Dried Mushrooms, Mineral Water, Wine.[/*]
[*][b]Group 2[/b]: Berry Liqueur, Gems, Juice, Meads, Minerals.[/*]
[*][b]Group 3[/b]: Aged Roe, Caviar, Gourmet Shellfish, Jelly, Pickles.[/*]
[*][b]Group 4[/b] (the fastest): Aged Coffee, Aged Milk, Aged Triple Shot Espresso, Beer, Cheese, Cloth, Coffee, Dishes, Dried Chips, Feather Bundle, Flower Oil, Honey, Ink of the Abyss, Luxury Cloth, Mayonnaise, Oil, Pale Ale, Pu-erh Tea, Raisins, Royal Jelly, Smoked Cheese, Smoked Egg, Smoked Fish, Syrups, Tea, Triple Shot Espresso, Truffle Oil, Vinegar.[/*]
[/list]
[b]Configuration[/b]
You can configure the [b]speed[/b] at which Casks age each group of items. The higher the aging multiplier, the less time it takes for the product to age.[/spoiler]

[b]Machine Progression System is compatible with everything[/b], as it does not modify any vanilla assets or those of other mods, and only adds and builds on new content. It is safe to install alongside any mods and at any point in your playthrough. [b]It will never cause any conflicts or errors[/b].

However, I do not know if it works as intended with the [b]Android[/b] version of SMAPI. If the frameworks that Machine Progression System relies on—Content Patcher, Extra Machine Configs, Machine Terrain Framework, and Machine Upgrade System—work on Android, then Machine Progression System should as well.


[center][img]https://i.imgur.com/PckYXll.png[/img][/center]
After the 3.1 update, and thanks to [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/22256]Extra Machine Configs[/url]﻿, Machine Progression System copies the rules of the vanilla machines, which means that it [b]no longer requires compatibility patches and will accept any mod's items by default[/b]. After Extra Machine Configs copies the rules, Machine Progression System applies some configuration tokens on top so users can customize the outcome of the process.

If you have a lot of mods, I highly recommend also using [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/28261]Machine Control Panel[/url]. Many mods target the same vanilla processes—like making Juice or Wine—which can lead to conflicting rules. With Machine Control Panel, you can easily choose which rules you want your Machine Progression System machines to follow.

If you wish to know more about the customization process for modded items and are somewhat knowledgeable about modding, open the following spoiler. If you are usually overwhelmed by data or are uninterested in the process, forget all about it and enjoy the mod.

[spoiler]First of all, note that the way we are discussing these parameters [b]only applies to new items introduced by other mods[/b]. They [b]do not affect vanilla processes or MPS items, so MPS remains fully configurable[/b].

[b]Input quantity[/b]
Input quantities cannot be modified for modded items. This is barely a limitation, since most machine processes only take one item at a time. The issue comes with machines that take more than one item (namely the Dehydrator, Furnace and Slime Egg-Press). With those 3 machines I had a choice: apply a global token that would severely nerf or buff certain modded items or respect the original modder's concept. I chose the latter. This means that, even if you change the amount of input required for the Dehydrator in the config, it will not apply to modded items (it will still apply for vanilla processes or MPS items, though).

[b]Output quantity[/b]
Output quantities can be fully modified through the "Quantity" tokens and the "Bonus" tokens. However, when a machine has "Minimum Quantity" and "Maximum Quantity" tokens (Bait Maker, Bone Mill, Furnace, Recycling Machine, Seed Maker), only the "Minimum Quantity" token is applied to the modded item. Due to how the code is written, it is not possible to include both "Minimum Quantity" and "Maximum Quantity" at the same time, so the former was chosen to preserve balance for modded items.

[b]Output quality[/b]
Output quality can be fully modified through the "Quality" tokens. However, due to how the "Copy Quality" and "Quality" tokens interact, "Copy Quality" is always toggled on for modded items, even if it's unchecked in the config. In scenarios where both are applied, the machine will choose the highest-quality outcome. For example: if the machine outputs Gold-quality produce and the input is Silver-quality, the final product will be Gold-quality; if the machine outputs Silver-quality produce and the input is Gold-quality, the final product will be Gold-quality.

[b]Processing Time[/b]
Processing time can be fully modified through the "Production Time" token. However, when machines have more than one production time (namely the Furnace and the Keg), the processing time for modded items is determined by the value of the output item. Each value has a determined bracket that can be modified in the config. This is how each bracket has been assigned for every machine:

Furnace or Heavy Furnace
[spoiler]Modded items with a value between 0 and 119 follow the "Copper Production Time" token.
Modded items with a value between 120 and 249 follow the "Iron Production Time" token.
Modded items with a value between 250 and 999 follow the "Gold Production Time" token.
Modded items with a value between 1000 and 2999 follow the "Iridium Production Time" token.
Modded items with a value of 3000 or above follow the "Radioactive Production Time" token.[/spoiler]

Keg
[spoiler]Modded items with a value between 0 and 100 follow the "Coffee Production Time" token.
Modded items with a value between 101 and 300 follow the "Vinegar Production Time" token.
Modded items with a value between 301 and 600 follow the "Pale Ale Production Time" token.
Modded items with a value between 601 and 999 follow the "Mead Production Time" token.
Modded items with a value of 1000 or above follow the "Wine Production Time" token.[/spoiler]

[b]Bone Mill[/b]

 - If your custom item doesn't belong to any of the categories above and doesn't have any of the context tags mentioned, there are four context tags you can use: cask_group1_item, cask_group2_item, cask_group3_item and cask_group4_item. Group 1 is the one that takes the longest to age (like Wine) and Group 4 is the one that takes the shortest to age (like Cheese). Adding these context tags would automatically make your product ageable in the MPS casks.

 - The Crab Pot catches fish in the category_fish (-4).

 - The Furnaces can smelt any item in the category_gem (-2) and category_minerals (-12).

[b]Geode Crusher[/b]
 - If you want to add new drops for the different Geodes, you only need to make a patch that targets the RandomItemId section.

[b]Keg[/b]
 - The Keg can make Juice from any item in the category_vegetable (-75), category_greens (-81) or with the keg_juice context tag. It can also make Wine from any item in the category_fruits (-79) or with the keg_wine context tag. Additionally, you can make Berry Liqueur with any item with the berry_item context tag and Mineral Water with any item in the category_gem (-2) or category_minerals (-12).

[b]Loom[/b]
 - The Loom makes Feather Bundles from any item with the feather_item context tag.

[b]Mayonnaise Machine[/b]
 - The Mayonnaise Machine recognizes items with the large_egg_item or egg_item context tags, so make sure to use those appropriately.

[b]Mushroom Log[/b]
 - The Mushroom Log can output items with the tree_syrup_item context tag.

[b]Oil Maker[/b]
 - The Oil Maker makes Flower Oil from any item in the category_flowers (-80).

[b]Preserves Jar[/b]
 - The Preserves Jar makes Pickles from any item in the category_vegetable (-75), category_greens (-81) or with the preserves_pickle context tag. It can also make Jelly from any item in the category_fruits (-79) or with the preserves_Jelly context tag. Additionally, you can make Aged Milk with any items with the milk_item or large_milk_item context tags and Gourmet Shellfish from any items with the fish_crab_pot context tags.

[b]Recycling Machine[/b]
 - If you want to add new drops to the recycled Trash (item 168), you only need to make a patch that targets the RandomItemId section.

[b]Seed Maker[/b]
 - The Seed Maker makes seeds from any crop and Mixed Seeds from any item with the category_greens (-81).

[b]Slime Egg-Press[/b]
 - If you want to add new drops to the press, you only need to make a patch that targets the RandomItemId section.[/spoiler]

[quote]﻿Can you [b]integrate[/b] 'x' mod with Machine Progression System?[/quote]
Since the 3.1 version, Machine Progression System [b]no longer requires compatibility patches[/b]. Every mod is integrated by default.

[quote]﻿Can you create new upgrades for [b]machines added by other mods[/b]?[/quote]
[b]No[/b]. Machine Progression System only adds upgrades for the artisan and refining machines that are part of the base game. However, mod authors are welcome to create their own machine upgrades in line with MPS' philosophy.

[quote]Why does the Loom have a [b]machine for every tier[/b], while the Oil Maker only starts at Diamond?[/quote]
The Loom recipe does not require any of the materials used in the progression system—Iron Bars, Gold Bars, Diamonds, Iridium Bars, Radioactive Bars, or Prismatic Shards. On the other hand, the Oil Maker requires a Gold Bar, so it starts at the Diamond tier and skips the first two. I probably could have given every machine all seven tiers, but this approach made the most sense to me when I first designed MPS.

[quote]﻿Does it work with [b]Walk of Life[/b]?[/quote]
It does. However, if you want Walk of Life to affect MPS machines, you have to change something in the settings of Walk of Life, I believe. I can't help you with that, and probably neither will they, given how rude and unpleasant they are. I would rather use [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/20054]Vanilla Plus Professions[/url] (created by KediDili and Airyn), which is a way better mod and created by much nicer people.

[quote]﻿Can I use [b]Alternative Textures[/b] to change the appearance of the machines?[/quote]
That is something that needs to be done by the creator of the custom craftables skin. For Machine Progression System, it is preferred to have native skins that reflect the different upgrade tiers. Currently, there is native support for Gwen's Medieval Craftables and Nano's Craftables.
